A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same asynchronous test-time scaling framework, renamed from A1 to ATTS. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, latency, throughput, memory, budget-prediction, and multi-turn intervention results, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds OlympiadBench evaluation, scaling experiments, efficiency measurements, and a rejection-threshold ablation.

M1.justification: The online calibration, unnormalized conformity scores, conformal p-value rule, and draft/verification/target-continuation pipeline remain unchanged. ATTS is a renaming. Appendix A.5 newly evaluates conventional resampling against continuation, an alternative already distinguished from the proposed procedure in v1.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on harder Olympiad-level problems through OlympiadBench, while retaining MATH100, AMC23, AIME24, and AIME25. This is a limited coverage extension; the evaluated OlympiadBench subset is insufficiently specified to establish additional language or modality coverage.

E2.justification: The main SpecReason, SpecThink, and standalone draft/target baselines are retained. Appendix A.5 adds a standard-resampling comparison, and Figure 9 introduces o3-mini low/medium/high and GPT-5 reference levels. These plotted comparisons do not establish that the authors newly ran the closed-source models.

E3.justification: New protocols include a 1.5B/70B model pairing with 20 turns and up to 128 samples, a 15-turn OlympiadBench evaluation, and an AIME25 turn sweep. Tables 1–2 add configuration-level speedup and token-consumption ratios, and Figure 1 changes its concurrency grid. Section 4.4 also replaces the headline result's 8192-token description with an unlimited-turn description, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds accuracy/runtime sensitivity to alpha, accuracy versus sequential turns, large-scale sample-count analysis, and continuation-versus-resampling experiments. These test parameter choice, scaling saturation, and sampling tradeoffs absent from v1. The existing calibration-budget mismatch and perplexity/intervention analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the empirical results. The retained conformal coverage guarantees are method theory, rather than newly added experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive speedup, token-ratio, OlympiadBench, scaling, and ablation results. Existing results also change: Table 1's AMC23 conditional score for DeepSeek Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct/s1.1-32B changes from 93.0 to 96.0; Figure 6b's 64-sample, 500/700-token takeover rate changes from 28.4% to 25.8%. Table 2's original accuracy values remain unchanged after matching the reordered baseline columns.

T1.justification: Section 2 adds an explicit classical prediction-set definition in Equation 6 and an accompanying conditional-coverage assertion. The substantial theoretical development is retained: all four propositions, both theorems, their assumptions, and their proofs move unchanged from Appendix A.4 to A.8.

C1.justification: The central claims of asynchronous, training-free acceleration, rejection-rate control, and 56.7x speedup/4.14x throughput improvement remain. v3 adds an abstract-level claim that a 1.5B/70B combination reaches o3-mini (high) performance on AIME; Appendix A.5 associates that result with the resampling configuration.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands the discussion of when efficiency gains occur: longer draft reasoning can cause slowdowns, additional turns can reach an accuracy plateau, and resampling improves accuracy per nominal sample while consuming more tokens. It also interprets alpha's accuracy/runtime tradeoff and acknowledges computational limits on larger-scale evaluation. These add substantive applicability boundaries beyond v1's existing coverage and efficiency interpretations.

D1.justification: Appendix A.9 newly supplies completion and multiple-choice prompts, and Appendix A.4 newly states a default maximum of 10 turns. Settings for the added experiments are also documented. These additions do not establish changes to the earlier prompts or default implementation; the inference-engine version and code-access destination remain the same.

R1.justification: v3 adds references on conformal p-values and class-conditional prediction, including Bates, Ding, Jin and Candes, and Wang, and sharpens the distinction between ordinal scoring and normalized class probabilities. It also adds OlympiadBench and mathematical-reasoning references. The existing related-work section is otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 renames the framework, edits the abstract and introductory/method explanations, clarifies notation, and updates author and publication information. It adds acknowledgments and an LLM-use declaration, while retaining the main narrative order and most existing appendix prose.

P2.justification: Both principal tables are substantially redesigned with new efficiency columns, grouping, and highlighting. Memory and budget-prediction plots are redrawn, token consumption is reorganized into Figure 8, and new scaling/ablation plots and Table 3 are added. The original intervention figure is retained as Figure 11 rather than removed.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's accuracy-focused tables, v3 makes efficiency more assessable through per-configuration speedups and token ratios. New sensitivity and resampling studies expose useful cost and failure tradeoffs, while explicit prompts improve reproducibility. These benefits are tempered by insufficiently documented comparability with closed-source reference scores and the retained conflicting temperature descriptions. The empirical documentation improves, but the strongest claims remain incompletely qualified.
